spec.name: Transatlantic Four-Seat Tourer

assumptions: Cruise at L/D max = 11; loiter at 0.866 L/D max (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 3 (p. 22))
Loiter speed = 0.75 x cruise speed
Spar = 8.5% of statistical empty weight on lap 0 (Assumption (Spiral): not from a textbook table)
Cruise flown at 75% of installed power
Stall wing loading at ISA sea-level density (1.225 kg/m^3)
Ultimate manoeuvring load factor n_ult = 5.70
Cantilever wing root at y = 0 m; aero lift carried 100% by main spar
No inertia relief from wing structure or fuel (conservative)
Ultimate load = 1.5 x limit load (Raymer 2ed, p. 335)
Spar depth = 85% of local aerofoil thickness; cap width = 35% of depth
Caps sized at ultimate load to compression yield F_cy = 338 MPa (compression cap governs; crippling not modelled)
Tension cap margin against F_tu = 483 MPa: +0.57
Web: no shear failure (F_su = 234 MPa) and no shear buckling, unstiffened panel, K = 4.8 (classical long simply supported panel; Raymer gives K as a chart, Fig. 14.42)
Minimum gauges: cap >= 2.0 mm, web >= 1.5 mm (assumption)
Mass counts caps and web only: no stiffeners, ribs or fittings
Tail moment arm = 52% of fuselage length (Raymer 2ed Table 6.4 typical arm ratio)
Wing configuration: high wing
Lofted 12-vertex tapered I-beam across 21 spanwise stations (y = 0 to 7.58 m)
Includes 1.38x structural non-optimum mass factor for root carry-through fittings and web stiffeners
Clamped root boundary condition (w = 0, dw/dy = 0) at wing root y = 0 m
Timoshenko shear deformation factor Phi_e = 12*E*I / (G*A_web*L_e^2) per tapered element
3D von Mises stress recovery across outer flange fiber, web-flange fillet, and neutral axis
V_L in Eq. 14.12 taken as the spec cruise speed; the true maximum level speed is higher, so V_p and the tail load are underestimated
Manoeuvre load evaluated at sea-level density
Raymer's arbitrary tail C_n load treated as a limit load and multiplied by the ultimate factor 1.5
Each tail half is a cantilever from the fuselage centreline; the spar carries the whole tail load
Elevator-deflection load split (Fig. 14.14) and tail torsion not modelled
Tail spar uses the wing spar material and the same I-beam proportions (depth 85% of t, cap width 35% of depth)
Lofted 12-vertex tapered I-beam across 21 spanwise stations (y = 0 to 2.98 m)
Landing weight = MTOW (conservative; Raymer uses W_landing)
Tire deflection neglected in Eq. 11.12 (S_T = 0): gives a longer, conservative stroke
Oleo-pneumatic, fixed orifice, efficiency at the low end of Table 11.4 (0.65)
Wing lift = weight during stroke; the FAR-23 two-thirds rule is ignored, as Raymer allows for initial sizing (p. 242)
Main oleos carry 92% of the weight: nose share 8% at the most-aft c.g. (p. 233)
Spin-up, spring-back, braking and side loads not analysed
warnings: Web shear buckling sets the web thickness at 17 of 21 stations
Horizontal tail taper ratio 0.65 is outside 0.3-0.6 (Raymer 2ed, Table 4.3 (p. 76))
Web shear buckling sets the web thickness at 2 of 21 stations
